title: The written rules and the agents' context
grade_reasons: The base is sound: the rules in full already sit in files read on demand and a test keeps them out of the always-loaded file, 99.84% of the 3,145 code names they cite exist, and no doc reaches a deployment or a CI run. The waste is real: every session and subagent loads 44 KB where about 10 KB is needed (71% is an index of which a change needs 2 to 4 lines), the search tool cannot show 52% of the rules or 98% of the decisions, and 5 of 24 merges in 35 hours renumbered a decision. It is not a B because no budget exists at all and one test makes the always-loaded file grow (35% in 12 days); it is not a D because the surplus is about a fifth of what a median change reads, the costs are tokens and merge work, and nothing has to be rebuilt.

measures.name: Loaded into every session and every subagent
measures.today: CLAUDE.md is 43,361 bytes in 448 lines and imports AGENTS.md (679 bytes): about 11,000 tokens (estimate, 4 characters a token), loaded again after each compaction. 71% is a 295-line feature index; the median change needs 2 to 4 of its lines. Source: wc -c -l at HEAD; the docs-context digest.
measures.target_a: CLAUDE.md at most 10,500 bytes and 160 lines (about 2,600 tokens). AGENTS.md as Next.js writes it. No file in .claude/rules without a paths list. These are hard ceilings in the test, not a baseline that can be raised with a reason.
measures.how_measured: wc -c -l CLAUDE.md today. After work item 1: src/lib/docs-budget.scan.test.ts and node scripts/docs-ratchet.mjs --check, which .github/workflows/docs-budget.yml also runs on a docs-only push.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is what a session must know before it opens any file: the workflow, the stack, the commands, the never-sentences (no migration by hand, money in minor units, the VAT rate, no sign-in bypass, grounded AI, the name), Homer and Lisa, the platform rule and a map of the seven rule files. By the planner's section sizes that is about 9.5 KB: 12,555 bytes outside the index, less about 5 KB of how-to that belongs to folders, plus about 2 KB of map and look-ups. 10,500 is 10% above the floor. Under 15,000 (index out, how-to still in) is a B: it still loads database, e2e, typed-row and AI-eval how-to into sessions that touch none of them.

measures.name: Text a search cannot show (lines over 500 characters)
measures.today: docs/rules: 156 lines hold 291,981 of 564,581 bytes (52%). docs/decisions.md: 548 lines hold 97.8% of 1.33 MB. The other living docs: 731 lines, 602,672 bytes (11.7% of 5.1 MB) in 61 of 138 files; 321 are prose and 410 are table rows. CLAUDE.md: 1 line. The search tool prints '[Omitted long matching line]' for each. Source: awk at HEAD; my node count over git ls-files docs for the other docs.
measures.target_a: 0 in CLAUDE.md, docs/rules and docs/decisions. 0 prose lines in every other living doc. Table rows over 500 characters: at most 410, only falling, none in a new file.
measures.how_measured: awk 'length($0)>500' on the files today. After work items 1 and 12: scripts/lib/docs-count.mjs, held per file in src/lib/docs-budget.baseline.json by the scan test.
measures.why_this_is_a: CLAUDE.md tells sessions to find a rule by searching. A line the search cannot show is read whole (up to 18 KB) or missed. Prose can be wrapped by a script that proves no word changed, so its floor is 0. A Markdown table row cannot be wrapped: the 410 rows in finished specs (324 KB, under 5% of the living docs) are the stated tolerance. Stopping at the rules and the decisions is a B: the rules send sessions to those specs for the detail.

measures.name: Growth, and what checks it
measures.today: No budget exists. CLAUDE.md grew from 32 KB on 30 October to 43.4 KB (35% in 12 days, about 0.95 KB a day); docs/rules grew from 374 KB to 566 KB. rules-index.test.ts fails unless each new rule adds a line to CLAUDE.md. 24 rules are over 4,000 bytes (largest 11,209) and 46 decisions are (largest 17,985). 27 fixes of this review ask for a new sentence in CLAUDE.md. A docs-only push runs no check. Source: docs/consolidation.md:12-13; wc and my counts at HEAD; findings/*.json.
measures.target_a: Every number on this card is in one baseline file and checked on every push, docs-only ones too. CLAUDE.md cannot pass its ceiling. A new rule and a new decision are at most 4,000 bytes; the 24 and 46 older ones only fall. No test and no habit asks for a line in CLAUDE.md per rule, per budget or per tracker.
measures.how_measured: src/lib/docs-budget.scan.test.ts with src/lib/docs-budget.baseline.json, and .github/workflows/docs-budget.yml for pushes of Markdown alone (work item 1). Today: wc and the git history.
measures.why_this_is_a: The file was cut from 382 KB to 32 KB once and regrew by a third in 12 days. Without a ceiling every other measure here is spent again within weeks. The floor is one check per measure, run where docs change. The tolerance is the 24 old rules and 46 old decisions over 4,000 bytes: they are shortened when next edited, because a sweep risks losing a reason.

measures.today: docs: 22 of 225 files, 1.06 MB (10%), are dated reports, draft notes, review evidence and a generated report. supabase: 791 of 796 files, 7.3 MB, are archived migrations and Drizzle's snapshot. The floor is the four baseline SQL files, which stay searchable because functions, triggers and reference data live only there. Nothing is moved or deleted, so there is no tolerance to state: a default search skips these files or it does not.

measures.today: 5 of 3,145 code names cited in docs/rules no longer exist (0.16%). One copied list has drifted: 14 store features in code, 11 in the rule, 12 in the doc. CLAUDE.md sends architectural work to docs/plan.md (72.6 KB, written before multi-tenancy) and tells sessions to add to a Migration versions list frozen since 4 October. No test checks any of it. Source: the planner's name check; the files opened.
measures.target_a: 0 cited names missing, held by a scan test over every backticked name followed by a bracket. No copied list of ids where the code has the list. No standing instruction that points at a frozen or superseded file.
measures.how_measured: The name check added to src/lib/docs-budget.scan.test.ts (work item 6); rg for the two instructions (work items 6 and 8).
measures.why_this_is_a: A wrong rule costs more than a long one: the session acts on it. The floor is 0 and a test can hold it. 0.16% is already good work, but unheld it is a B: 34 decisions and their rules were added in 35 hours, and names move with them.

measures.name: Merges that renumber a decision
measures.today: 5 of 24 merges in 35 hours (116 commits, 10 sessions). 8 of 34 new decisions changed number, five of them twice. Two merges rewrote 64 and 77 files. docs/decisions.md is resolved by hand in 6 of 24 merges. Source: git log --merges at HEAD (the 5 confirmed by me).
measures.target_a: 0 in 100 consecutive commits on main. No decision id twice, held by a test. After the split, two sessions cannot conflict in one table.
measures.how_measured: git log --merges --format=%s over the last 100 commits on main, searched for 'renumber', 'taken on main' and 'decision is D'; the duplicate-id check in src/lib/decisions.scan.test.ts.
measures.why_this_is_a: Each collision is a merge across up to 77 source files, a second run of the checks, and a chance that a comment now cites another session's decision. A number claimed on main before it is cited makes the floor 0. There is no tolerance: the cost rises with the number of sessions at once.

measures.name: What a session is told to read before it starts
measures.today: Architectural work: docs/plan.md, 72,617 bytes (about 18,000 tokens). A code review fix: a Progress table with 16,641 bytes of notes in 18 rows (15 over 500 characters), growing about 0.9 KB a step. A PSI item: 60,043 bytes to find 12 open items of 2,428 bytes. One decision: two calls and 1,940 bytes at the median, 17,985 at most. This review's plan will be a third tracker. Source: wc at HEAD; the digest.
measures.target_a: No standing instruction sends a session to more than 20 KB. Every tracker row is at most 300 characters (status, date, commit, decision). A tracker's open items sit in one section. A decision is one file found by one search, with an index row under 200 characters.
measures.how_measured: wc -c on the files CLAUDE.md names; the tracker-row check in src/lib/docs-budget.scan.test.ts (work item 7) and src/lib/decisions.scan.test.ts (work item 10).
measures.why_this_is_a: These loads are ordered by the instructions, so they are paid whenever the instruction is followed. docs/platform.md, the note on how the platform is built, is 16 KB: that sets the 20 KB bar. A tracker needs a step's status, date and commit; the story belongs in the decision. Shorter notes without a check are a B: the code review's own rule already asked for a date and a commit, and its notes still grew to 925 bytes a row.

measures.name: What a session really loads (measured, not estimated)
measures.today: Not measured. Every figure on this card is a file size or an estimate at 4 characters a token. The proxy: the median code change touches source files of 143 KB together (p75 798 KB). It is not known whether a session reads one rule (median 1.4 KB) or its whole file (49 to 163 KB). 15 non-test source files are over 100 KB and 11 are over 2,000 lines; nothing holds either count. Source: the digest; my wc over git ls-files at HEAD.
measures.target_a: A sample of 20 working sessions shows: written rules and docs read per code change at most 25 KB at the median (the 10.5 KB core, one list of an area's headings, two rules); no read of a rule file or of the decisions index over 20 KB; no '[Omitted long matching line]' from docs/rules or docs/decisions. The counts of source files over 100 KB (15) and over 2,000 lines (11) are in the code ratchet and only fall.
measures.how_measured: scripts/session-load.mjs over session transcripts (the JSONL files under ~/.claude/projects), created by work item 13 and run again at each quarterly squash; the two file counts in src/server/ratchet.baseline.json.
measures.why_this_is_a: An A needs a figure from real use, as other areas have production figures: the tests above hold file sizes, not what sessions do with them. 25 KB is the sum of what a change needs once the other measures are met, so the tolerance is inside that sum. For source files the floor is a holder, not a number: a large file is read by window, so its size is not all loaded, and the splits are the code review's steps 3.2, 3.13 and 3.14.

work_items.title: Shorten each rule and decision over 4,000 bytes when it is next changed (DC-4 step 5)
work_items.done_when: The baseline's counts of rules over 4,000 bytes (24 today) and decisions over 4,000 bytes (46 today) have only fallen, and an edited rule no longer opens by repeating its heading (292 of 295 do today).
work_items.moves: Growth: the stated tolerance of 24 rules and 46 decisions shrinks; a rule read before a change costs at most 4 KB instead of up to 11 KB.

tolerated.why: The parity-wave workflow has not run since feature waves were paused on 29 October, so no session pays for it. Its fix is three edits (cap the spec at 30,000 characters; tell agents to read sections 1 to 5 and their own part; drop the draft of a CLAUDE.md bullet) to make on the day a wave is next run. Left as it is, a run would cost about 270,000 tokens (the skeptic's estimate).

owner_choices.question: Do you read the parity report's detail tables on GitHub? If not, docs/shopify-parity.md can keep its five summary blocks (under 30 KB, 289 KB today) and pnpm parity prints the rest. If you do, it stays as it is and only leaves default searches.

For work items 3 and 11 (DC-1; the code review's question 5): CLAUDE.md is your instruction file. May its 295-line feature index go, leaving a map of the seven rule files and a three-line look-up (44 KB to under 15 KB per session)? And may the database, e2e, typed-row and AI-eval how-to then load only when those folders are opened (to under 10.5 KB)? The second can be declined on its own. Without the first this area cannot reach an A.

For work item 8 (DC-10): after a migration, should 'advisors checked, nothing new' still be written down? The check itself stays either way. Today the note goes into decision rows: 205 of 564 mention the advisors.

Should this plan get lines of its own in CLAUDE.md, as the code review has (the draft's question 10)? Proposed: no. One shared line names the trackers (the code review, the PSI follow-ups, this plan), and each tracker keeps its rules at its own top.
